text:
harper: New hire report: the CLI onboarding hit multiple snags. Installed redwoodctl via brew on mac, then ran through quickstart and got stuck on auth + completions. Posting notes so we can triage.

harper: Steps: brew install redwood && redwoodctl login --headless && redwoodctl config profile create my-team && ./quickstart/start.sh

harper: Problems observed: (1) `redwoodctl login --headless` tried to open a browser in our SSH session (no browser available) and then timed out after 45s. (2) zsh completions were not active even after reinstall; `redwoodctl --help` didn't show subcommands. (3) the profile create command created both "my-team" and a new "default" with identical creds.

din: thanks for the repro. For (1) the headless flow should detect no-tty and fall back to device-code. Looks like our detection missed SSH sessions where TERM is set but no DISPLAY. We should check isatty on stdin/stdout, not just TERM.

mike: (2) completions are a pain. Our Homebrew formula currently installs completions under the cellars dir but doesn't `brew link` them for non-cask installs, so users on mac who rely on their shell's completion path won't see them. Also our postinstall expects completions/_redwoodctl to exist in the build artifact but the makefile recently changed output paths.

din: for the profile duplication: I dug into the merge logic in config.Load(). If REDWOOD_PROFILE is set and the named profile doesn't exist, config.Init() creates the new profile AND unconditionally writes a fallback default pointer. That creates two entries. Simpler fix: if env-profile missing, create only the named profile and set it as active; do not create default unless user explicitly asks.

ops: cross-platform note: on Windows MSI we got reports of the installer writing the credentials file with read-only attributes when installed to ProgramData and then failing token refresh. Also in headless Win containers the login tried to spawn explorer which fails. We should: ensure installer sets user-writable perms for credential files and never attempt GUI launch if no interactive session.

mike: small DX suggestion: add `--no-browser` flag and `--output json|plain` for auth flows. The JSON output should include flow type, url, and user_code so automation can pick it up. Also prefer device-code if stdout is not a tty.

harper: yes, that would have saved new hire time. They had to paste codes into a browser on their phone and the CLI kept waiting for a browser callback that never arrived.

din: auth retry behavior: we currently retry refresh token request 5x with exponential backoff before failing. In CI that blocks pipelines for minutes. Proposal: if not interactive -> do 0 retries and exit with code 74 AUTH_REQUIRED and a machine-readable hint; if interactive -> 1 quick retry then prompt.

mike: also note token expiration handling: CLI sometimes treats a valid token as expired because the server returned 401 during short signing key rotation. We should do a single immediate refresh attempt on 401, and if refresh fails with 5xx treat as transient and surface a short-lived error instead of looping. Avoid long blocking loops.

ops: localserve/quic dev note: the local auth proxy currently honors REDWOOD_BIND_HOST only when --allow-public is passed; env var ignored. This broke our devcontainer tests because we want explicit 0.0.0.0 bind for container-local workflows. Let's respect REDWOOD_BIND_HOST env var and print a warning if it exposes a public interface.

harper: config parse nit: some users include comments in ~/.redwood/config. Our strict JSON parser fails with an opaque parse error. We should accept JSONC-like comments for the user config file (strip // and /* */) or at minimum give a clear error recommending jsonc or removing comments.

din: agree, but keep programmatic parsing strict when REDWOOD_CONFIG_PATH is set (CI). Only lenient for the default user path. Add tests.

mike: packaging edge: alpine containers fail due to glibc dependency. For localtest images we should publish a musl build or static binary. Short-term doc note telling users to use Debian-slim images or install gcompat.

ops: proposed action items: 1) detect non-tty & auto-fallback to device-code; add `--no-browser` and `--output json`; 2) fix completion packaging + brew linking + postinstall path; 3) change config create/merge to prefer env-specified profile and avoid creating default; 4) tune auth retries for non-interactive flows + single immediate refresh on 401; 5) respect REDWOOD_BIND_HOST in localserve; 6) accept JSONC for user config; 7) publish musl/static binaries for alpine.

dev-bot: Created issues: #4801 (auth: no-tty device-code auto-fallback + --no-browser + json output), #4802 (packaging: completions path & brew link), #4803 (config: env profile create duplicate), #4804 (auth: retry tuning & single refresh on 401), #4805 (localserve: honor REDWOOD_BIND_HOST), #4806 (config: support JSONC user config), #4807 (build: musl/static binary for alpine).

harper: thanks all. I'll attach the new hire's console transcript to #4801 and validate once PRs land. :sparkles:
